title: Water Margin (Shuihu zhuan)
summary: Water Margin is a Chinese vernacular novel about outlaws who gather at a mountain stronghold in Shandong under Song Jiang. The story is set in the twelfth century and took its final form in the fourteenth, according to a reference entry; the Library of Congress places its writing in the early Ming and ascribes it traditionally to Shi Naian and Luo Guanzhong.

uncertainty.note: EBSCO says final form in the fourteenth century; the Library of Congress says early Ming (from 1368). The range 1368-1400 is the overlap; authorship and exact date are traditional or uncertain.

as_recorded.value: put into its final form in the fourteenth
Written in the early Ming Dynasty

where.modern_name: Shandong province, China (region centre; labelled proxy pin for the story's setting)
where.historical_name: Shandong, Ming empire (setting of the outlaws' stronghold)

importance.justification: One of the major Chinese vernacular novels, drawing on twelfth-century outlaw stories, and a long-lived source of later Chinese drama and art (Library of Congress; EBSCO).

reviewer_note: Date and authorship are contested: EBSCO says final form in the 14th century and does not name authors; LOC says traditional ascription to Shi Naian and Luo Guanzhong, written in early Ming; Britannica (not fetchable) reportedly says the text cannot be dated. I used the overlap 1368-1400. LOC calls Liangshan Marsh fictional, so the pin is the Shandong region centre (EBSCO places the lair in Shandong mountains), a labelled proxy.
